newsitem.title: USA: Clinton to meet Democrats Weds/Thurs on budget.
newsitem.headline: Clinton to meet Democrats Weds/Thurs on budget.

text.p: President Clinton will meet Democrats from the House and Senate Budget Committees on Wednesday and Thursday to discuss efforts to reach a five-year agreement on balancing the federal budget, Office of Management and Budget spokesman Lawrence Haas said Tuesday.

"He would not consider making a deal without soliciting their input, sounding them out and taking their views into account," Haas said when asked about reports that a budget agreement with Republicans was imminent.
Haas told Reuters the administration did not consider any date to be a deadline for reaching an agreement.
On Capitol Hill, a Democratic source said the party's lawmakers want to use the meeting to tell the White House what they can and cannot accept in a budget deal.
"Democrats are drawing the line in the sand," the source said.
Formal talks between the White House and Congress were expected to resume Wednesday. The negotiators took a break for the Jewish Passover holiday after nearly two weeks of daily meetings.

A spokeswoman for Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott said he has consisently sought more movement in the negotiations. The Mississippi Republican said over the weekend he was optimistic on chances for a deal.
"I think we can come to an agreement," Lott said on CNN's Late Edition program with Frank Sesno, adding that he believed it was important to move quickly. "I think the iron is hot."

Republicans have cited progress in the talks on ways to trim Medicare spending by at least $100 billion over the five years. At the same time, Democrats have insisted Republicans must now accept lower tax cuts. Senate Minority Leader Tom Daschle, Democrat of South Dakota, has said his party would accept no greater than $100 billion in tax cuts through 2002.
